Quasi-periodic libration point orbits are targeted under a high-fidelity model of the dynamics. Almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees are attained, as shown through Lyapunov's stability theory. Saturation of the actuators is formally included in the controller design, such that these guarantees hold even in the event of saturation. The relationship between saturation threshold, control gains, and deviation is studied and an optimal procedure for gain selection is discussed. The control solution is tested numerically through a Monte Carlo analysis over representative application cases, subject to operational errors, constraints, and external perturbations. Station-keeping under actuation saturation is validated considering a conservative threshold for typical electric propulsion systems.

AI.tldr: Novel nonlinear backstepping control for continuous low-thrust station-keeping in Earth-Moon system with quasi-periodic libration point orbits, featuring almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees that hold even under actuator saturation.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust station-keeping control solution for continuous low-thrust spacecraft in the Earth-Moon system that can handle the complex dynamics of quasi-periodic libration point orbits while accounting for practical limitations like actuator saturation and operational constraints.
AI.method: Nonlinear backstepping control law designed for high-fidelity dynamics model, incorporating actuator saturation formally into controller design. Uses Lyapunov stability theory to prove almost global uniform exponential stability. Includes analysis of saturation threshold, control gains, and deviation relationships with optimal gain selection procedure.
AI.result: Achieved almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees that hold even during actuator saturation events. Validated through Monte Carlo analysis over representative application cases with operational errors, constraints, and external perturbations. Demonstrated station-keeping capability with conservative saturation thresholds typical for electric propulsion systems.
AI.conclusion: The proposed nonlinear backstepping control provides a robust solution for continuous low-thrust station-keeping in the Earth-Moon system, with formal stability guarantees that account for practical actuator limitations and operational constraints, making it suitable for real-world spacecraft applications.

title: A Nonlinear Separation Principle: Applications to Neural Networks, Control and Learning
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2604.00119
summary: This paper investigates continuous-time and discrete-time firing-rate and Hopfield recurrent neural networks (RNNs), with applications in nonlinear control design and implicit deep learning. First, we introduce a nonlinear separation principle that guarantees global exponential stability for the interconnection of a contracting state-feedback controller and a contracting observer, alongside parametric extensions for robustness and equilibrium tracking. Second, we derive sharp linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions that guarantee the contractivity of both firing rate and Hopfield neural network architectures. We establish structural relationships among these certificates-demonstrating that continuous-time models with monotone non-decreasing activations maximize the admissible weight space, and extend these stability guarantees to interconnected systems and Graph RNNs. Third, we combine our separation principle and LMI framework to solve the output reference tracking problem for RNN-modeled plants. We provide LMI synthesis methods for feedback controllers and observers, and rigorously design a low-gain integral controller to eliminate steady-state error. Finally, we derive an exact, unconstrained algebraic parameterization of our contraction LMIs to design highly expressive implicit neural networks, achieving competitive accuracy and parameter efficiency on standard image classification benchmarks.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a contraction-based framework for stability analysis and control design of recurrent neural networks, introducing a nonlinear separation principle, LMI conditions for contractivity, and applications to control and implicit deep learning.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous stability guarantees and control design methods for recurrent neural networks (both firing-rate and Hopfield types) that can be applied to nonlinear control problems and implicit deep learning architectures, addressing the need for provable stability in RNN-based systems.
AI.method: Develops a contraction theory framework with: 1) a nonlinear separation principle for interconnected contracting systems, 2) sharp LMI conditions for contractivity of RNN architectures, 3) structural analysis of weight space admissibility, 4) extension to Graph RNNs, 5) LMI synthesis methods for controllers and observers, 6) low-gain integral control design, and 7) unconstrained parameterization of contraction LMIs for implicit neural networks.
AI.result: Establishes global exponential stability guarantees for interconnected contracting systems, derives exact LMI conditions for RNN contractivity, shows continuous-time models with monotone activations maximize admissible weight space, solves output reference tracking for RNN-modeled plants, and achieves competitive accuracy on image classification benchmarks with parameter-efficient implicit networks.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive contraction-based framework that unifies stability analysis, control design, and neural network architecture design, offering rigorous guarantees for RNN-based systems while enabling expressive implicit neural networks with competitive performance on standard benchmarks.

title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control
summary: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: Tube-based robust data-driven predictive control using single noisy trajectory with simplex constraint on Hankel coefficients, yielding convex QP with recursive feasibility and stability guarantees.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust predictive control scheme that requires only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown LTI system, without needing explicit system identification, while providing formal robustness guarantees against measurement noise.
AI.method: Imposes simplex constraint on Hankel coefficient vector to obtain explicit polyhedral bounds on prediction mismatch from bounded noise. Uses certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets to derive tube-tightened formulation. Online optimization becomes strictly convex quadratic program (QP).
AI.result: Controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input/state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples demonstrate effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance.
AI.conclusion: Proposed tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme provides formal robustness guarantees using only noisy trajectory data, with computationally tractable convex QP implementation and stability properties.
